official_source_semantics.caveat: Code semantics are source-audited. Only the captured r_01_gl/0001_data.mat sample values were numerically checked; other frames/recordings were not opened.

supported: The provided g1 summary names a same-recording block/r_01_gl H5/MAT pair and reports exact 717-to-717 event matching, all 717 spatial/polarity matches within 20 us, and zero nearest-time error; local script independently checks window/label arithmetic and count consistency.
The official E-POSE block.xyz and wood_block nontextured PLY are the same ordered point cloud to 1e-8 m, establishing a strong exact CAD correspondence for the block object.
The MAT pose and 3-D keypoint coordinates are geometrically self-consistent with that CAD point-cloud AABB to below 17 micrometres.

The stored 2-D keypoints align with the source's shared-depth projection plus undistortion (mean residual reported below 0.2 px), while correct per-point pinhole projection differs by about 16 px mean and up to 33 px; this strongly confirms the suspected common-depth bug in the saved 2-D labels.
The source exporter assigns cameraPose from frame index 2 inside the sample loop; that is a confirmed exporter bug/risk for later MAT rows of this moving sequence.
not_claimed: No raw H5/MAT binaries were re-read locally; exact event matching is cited from the captured g1 sample-audit summary, while geometry was recomputed from captured MAT values and local CAD files.
No real model inference, training, or real scoring occurred.
No statement that the fixed cameraPose is wrong for this particular first sample; one sample is internally consistent.
conclusion.recommended_data_handling: Keep the source MAT/H5 immutable. For any downstream pose supervision/evaluation, recompute 2-D projections from verified CAD points and MAT pose/K rather than consume suspect keypointprojections(:,1:2); use pose as the primary transform only after sample-wise convention checks, and do not use cameraPose until per-sample semantics are resolved.
